tests.name: session is still valid just before 15 minutes
tests.rule: session expires after 15 minutes
tests.setup: injected fake clock at T0; create session

tests.expected: session valid

tests.name: session expires after 15 minutes
tests.rule: session expires after 15 minutes
tests.setup: injected fake clock at T0; create session
tests.action: advance the clock past T0 + 15 min and check the session
tests.expected: session expired

spec_findings: The spec does not say whether a session is expired at exactly 15:00.000 or only after it; the boundary instant is left out of the tests until the owner decides.
defects: The test is nondeterministic: it waits on real setTimeout and compares two real Date.now() readings, so timer drift and scheduling make it fail about once in 20 runs. If the session code reads Date.now() directly with no injectable clock, that is a testability defect for the implementer.
covered: with a fixed clock, no real waiting
not_covered: the exact 15-minute instant, pending the spec finding
actions_now: Decline retry(3): a flaky test is a failing test until its cause is found, and the cause here is the real clock. Rewrite the test on a fake clock (fake timers or an injected clock) and tell the tech lead why.
